Side-by-side DNA and original Atlas reference. Blend is off initially; enabling it overlays the selected guide in the DNA panel while the original reference stays visible.

Original 24-position period grid: turn = period_index / 24.
Original nine-position residue grid: turn = residue / 9; path starts at 4.
One complete DNA window occupies one turn; both layers start at north and run clockwise.
Atlas node offsets equal native turn * full window length. Blended line shows node positions only, without connecting arcs.
DNA anchors use residue / 9 turns; each Atlas guide retains its native 9- or 24-position grid. Angular alignment does not equate a period index with a residue value.

Deliberate exact-position selection opens all records at that centre, with original intervals and evidence. No automatic record selection on initial load.
Coloured paths retain Atlas geometry; they do not represent measured movement or a temporal binding sequence.
Orange diamonds for interval-centre anchors. Short orange marks retain interval widths. Published elements are labelled US-1 and US-2.
Linear zero-based observation-count scale. Counts represent pooled observations at interval centres, not the number of distinct binding sites.
All sources use the same 39,248-base OXTR gene-plus-flanks window. JASPAR pools motif models; ENCODE pools targets and experimental cell contexts. The study set is incomplete.

Observations are grouped only by identical anchor_offset_bp. Neighbouring bases remain separate. Marks retain exact full-window coordinates.

Full window by default. Busiest-region zoom uses the most populated of 72 fixed sections solely to select a visible range; it does not combine centre counts. Selected-centre zoom shows 50 bases on either side. The origin and M9 mapping never change.
Visual exploration. No positional tolerance, association statistic, matched-control test or biological prediction accuracy has been evaluated.
